mainTopic: Acquiring a שטר and coins אגב קרקע, and what is included when selling a ship, a wagon or a yoke
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge to רב אשי, who holds that a שטר cannot be handed over through words alone. Two משניות show that a שטר is acquired automatically once the buyer takes possession of land. The גמרא answers that acquiring along with land (אגב) is a special, powerful method. Even coins, which cannot be acquired through חליפין, can be acquired אגב קרקע, as a story about רב פפא sending money through רב שמואל בר אחא shows. The גמרא then explains that the אנתיקי left out of a ship sale is the merchandise on board. A new משנה teaches that a wagon and its mules, or a yoke and its oxen, are sold separately. It also brings a dispute: רבי יהודה says the price can show what was meant, and חכמים say it cannot. The גמרא settles a ברייתא that seems to contradict the משנה by setting it in a case where the mules are harnessed to the wagon. It then explains that the price dispute applies where the word צמדא can mean either the yoke or the oxen. The amud ends with a challenge to חכמים: if the price is not proof, the sale should be cancelled. That challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two משניות show a document can be acquired along with land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings two משניות showing that a שטר is acquired automatically once the buyer takes possession of land. This challenges רב אשי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what we learned: a scribe may write a deed for the seller even when the buyer is not there. Once the buyer takes possession of the land, the deed becomes his wherever it is. And this is what we learned elsewhere: movable property can be acquired together with land, through money, a document, or taking possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is challenging רב אשי. It cites two משניות showing that a שטר becomes the buyer's automatically once he acquires the land, with no special act done to the document itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי held that a שטר cannot be transferred just by words. The first משנה says the deed is acquired 'wherever it is' as soon as the buyer takes the land, so nobody hands the document over. The second משנה gives the general rule behind this: movables (נכסים שאין להן אחריות) can be acquired along with land.

keyTerms.meaning: A document, here a deed of sale
Took possession (made a חזקה on the land)
Property with no guarantee, meaning movable property
Property that serves as a guarantee, meaning land
Acquiring land by doing an act of ownership on it

steps.confusionAlert: נכסים שיש להן אחריות means land, because a lender can collect from land that was sold. It does not mean property that comes with a warranty.

phrases.english: Like that which we learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה later in בבא בתרא (167b).

phrases.english: A document may be written for the seller

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹקֵחַ עִמּוֹ.
phrases.english: even if the buyer is not with him.
Once this one has taken possession of the land,
the document is acquired wherever it is;
and this is what we learned:
property that does not serve as a guarantee

phrases.aramaic: נִקְנִין עִם נְכָסִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן אַחְרָיוּת,
phrases.english: is acquired together with property that serves as a guarantee,
through money, a document, or taking possession!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the challenge to רב אשי from the earlier part of the daf
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's view that a שטר cannot be transferred through words alone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a שטר is acquired automatically with land, with no act done to the document itself, then a document can change hands without its own act of acquisition, and so surely through words as well.

steps.title: Acquiring along with land is a special method
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that אגב is a unique way of acquiring. Even coins, which cannot be acquired through חליפין, can be acquired אגב קרקע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Acquiring 'along with' land is different. Coins cannot be acquired through חליפין, yet they can be acquired along with land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אשי. It says the משניות only show that אגב works, not that plain words work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אגב is a strong method of its own and works even where other methods fail. The proof is coins: they cannot be acquired through חליפין, yet they can be acquired אגב קרקע. So a שטר acquired אגב קרקע says nothing about transferring a שטר through words.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Along with'; acquiring movables together with land
Acquisition by symbolic exchange, usually handing over a cloth

phrases.english: 'Along with' is different;
for a coin, which cannot be acquired through exchange,
yet it is acquired along with land.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: אגב is a unique method of acquisition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משניות seemed to prove that a שטר can be transferred with no act done to the document itself, so words should work too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only אגב, a special strong method, works for the שטר. That does not prove words would work.
steps.whatToRemember: אגב קרקע is a powerful method. It works even for coins, which cannot be acquired through חליפין.

steps.title: רב פפא transfers distant money through his threshold
steps.stepSummary: A story shows coins being acquired אגב קרקע. רב פפא transferred money held far away to רב שמואל בר אחא along with the threshold of his house.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the case of רב פפא, who had twelve thousand זוז in בי חוזאי. He transferred them to רב שמואל בר אחא along with the threshold of his house. When רב שמואל בר אחא came back, רב פפא went out to meet him as far as תווך.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real case to support the rule that coins can be acquired אגב קרקע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's money was far away in בי חוזאי, so he could not hand it over. He gave רב שמואל בר אחא a tiny piece of land, the threshold of his house, and the coins went along with it. That let רב שמואל בר אחא collect the money as its owner. רב פפא's happy trip out to meet him shows that the plan worked.

keyTerms.meaning: A distant region where the money was held

phrases.english: Like this case of Rav Pappa:
he had twelve thousand zuz
in Bei Chozai,

phrases.aramaic: אַקְנִינְהוּ נִיהֲלֵיהּ לְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַחָא
phrases.english: he transferred them to Rav Shmuel bar Acha
along with the threshold of his house.
When he came,
phrases.notes: This is רב שמואל בר אחא coming back with the money.

phrases.english: he went out to meet him as far as Tavakh.
phrases.notes: רב פפא is the one who went out, happy to have his money back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the rule from step 2 that coins are acquired אגב קרקע
steps.raayaObject: Coins can be acquired אגב קרקע
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of רב פפא transferring his twelve thousand zuz through his threshold
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that אגב can transfer property that is far away, because the movables do not need to be next to the land.

steps.title: Returning to the משנה about selling a ship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: someone who sells a ship has not sold the slaves, the packing bags, or the אנתיקי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he has not sold the slaves, nor the packing bags, nor the אנתיקי, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a new line of the משנה about selling a ship. This sets up a question about one unclear word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists items that are not included in the sale of a ship unless the seller says 'the ship and everything in it.' The word אנתיקי is unclear, so the גמרא will ask about it next.

keyTerms.meaning: A term the גמרא will explain next

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא מָכַר לֹא אֶת הָעֲבָדִים
phrases.english: But he has not sold the slaves
nor the packing bags
nor the antikei, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל לֹא מָכַר לֹא אֶת הָעֲבָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of אגב and returns to the ship משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Selling a ship does not include the slaves, packing bags, or אנתיקי.

steps.title: What does אנתיקי mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the word אנתיקי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question about what an unclear word in the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request for information, not an attack. We need to know what אנתיקי means in order to know what is left out of the ship sale.

phrases.english: What is 'antikei'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the משנה quoted in step 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word אנתיקי

steps.title: רב פפא: the merchandise on the ship
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that אנתיקי means the merchandise on board the ship.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: it means the merchandise that is inside the ship.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question: אנתיקי is the cargo the ship is carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the משנה teaches that selling a ship does not include its cargo. The goods are a separate business, not part of the ship.
steps.whatToRemember: Selling a ship does not include the merchandise on it (אנתיקי) unless the seller says 'everything in it.'

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The merchandise that is inside it.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אנתיקי means the merchandise carried on the ship.

steps.title: Selling a wagon or a yoke does not include the animals
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that selling a wagon does not include the mules, and selling a yoke does not include the oxen. The reverse is also true.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who sold a wagon has not sold the mules. Someone who sold the mules has not sold the wagon. Someone who sold a yoke has not sold the oxen. Someone who sold the oxen has not sold the yoke.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists items that are used together but are still sold separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wagon and the mules that pull it are two separate things, so naming one does not transfer the other. The same goes for the yoke and the oxen. This follows the same idea as the ship case in the earlier משנה: the main item is sold, but things connected to it are not automatically included.

keyTerms.meaning: Mules, the animals that pull the wagon
A yoke, the wooden frame placed on plowing animals

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who sold the wagon
has not sold the mules;
one who sold the mules
has not sold the wagon.
One who sold the yoke
has not sold the oxen;
one who sold the oxen
has not sold the yoke.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה continuing the list of what is included in a sale, after the ship case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wagon and its mules, or a yoke and its oxen, are each sold separately. Selling one does not include the other.

steps.title: Does the price show what was sold?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the price shows what was sold: if someone paid 200 זוז for a 'yoke', he clearly meant the oxen too. חכמים say the price is not proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: The price tells you what was sold. How so? If the buyer said, 'Sell me your yoke for two hundred זוז,' everyone knows a yoke is not worth two hundred זוז. And חכמים say: The price is not proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a dispute about whether the amount of money paid can show what the buyer really meant to buy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain yoke is cheap, so a price of 200 זוז only makes sense if the oxen are included. רבי יהודה lets the price tell us what the buyer meant. חכמים do not let the price decide what was sold.

keyTerms.meaning: The price tells us what was meant

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: The money makes it known.
How so? If he said to him:
'Sell me your yoke for two hundred zuz,'

phrases.aramaic: הַדָּבָר יָדוּעַ שֶׁאֵין הַצֶּמֶד בְּמָאתַיִם זוּז.
phrases.english: it is known that a yoke does not cost two hundred zuz.
And the Sages say: The money is not proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a dispute to the yoke case of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: the price can show that the oxen were included. חכמים: the price proves nothing.

steps.title: A ברייתא says selling the wagon includes the mules
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא from ארץ ישראל teaches a ברייתא before רבי אבהו: selling a wagon does include the mules.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב תחליפא from the West taught before רבי אבהו: One who sold the wagon has sold the mules.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the opposite of our משנה. It is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said the mules are not included, but this ברייתא says they are. That clash is what the next steps will deal with.

keyTerms.meaning: Before him, in front of him

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ תָּנֵי רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר מַעְרְבָא
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Taḥlifa from the West taught
phrases.notes: 'The West' means ארץ ישראל, which lies west of בבל.

phrases.english: before Rabbi Abbahu:

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר אֶת הַקָּרוֹן – מָכַר אֶת הַפְּרָדוֹת.
phrases.english: One who sold the wagon has sold the mules.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר מַעְרְבָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict the first ruling of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the ברייתא, selling a wagon includes the mules.

steps.title: But our משנה says the mules are not sold
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו objects: we learned in the משנה that the mules are not sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: 'he has not sold'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו points out that the ברייתא contradicts our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'he has sold the mules' and the משנה says 'he has not sold the mules.' Both cannot be true in the same case.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, used to start a challenge

phrases.english: But we learned 'he has not sold'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא from step 9 using the משנה from step 7
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא directly contradicts the משנה's ruling that the mules are not sold with the wagon.

steps.title: Should I erase the ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא asks רבי אבהו whether he should erase the ברייתא since it disagrees with the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Should I erase it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב תחליפא asks whether the ברייתא should be thrown out because it clashes with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה carries more weight than a ברייתא. So if they truly conflict, removing the ברייתא would be one way to solve the problem.

phrases.english: He said to him: Should I erase it?
phrases.notes: רב תחליפא is asking whether he should take this ברייתא out of what he teaches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge by suggesting the ברייתא be removed
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ברייתא is wrong and should be erased

steps.title: Keep the ברייתא: it is about mules tied to the wagon
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says not to erase it. The ברייתא is talking about mules that are harnessed to the wagon.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No. Explain your ברייתא as talking about mules that are fastened to it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו saves the ברייתא by placing it in a different case from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the mules are harnessed to the wagon, they count as part of it, so they are sold with it. The משנה is talking about mules that are not harnessed. Now there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Explain it, set it in a certain case

steps.whatToRemember: Mules harnessed to the wagon are sold with it (ברייתא). Mules that are not harnessed are not sold with it (משנה).

phrases.english: He said to him: No,
explain your baraita as dealing with mules fastened to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects erasing the ברייתא and answers the contradiction instead
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the two sources in different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and the משנה disagree, so the ברייתא must be wrong
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about mules harnessed to the wagon. The משנה is about mules that are not harnessed.

steps.title: Back to the yoke and oxen case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's yoke case to begin discussing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who sold the yoke has not sold the oxen, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה. It is setting up a question about this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'and so on' include the whole dispute between רבי יהודה and חכמים about the price. That dispute is what the גמרא is about to examine.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on, meaning the rest of the quoted text

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר אֶת הַצֶּמֶד – לֹא מָכַר אֶת הַבָּקָר וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: One who sold the yoke has not sold the oxen, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָכַר אֶת הַצֶּמֶד – לֹא מָכַר אֶת הַבָּקָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the wagon case to the yoke case of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Selling the yoke does not include the oxen, and רבי יהודה and חכמים argue about the price.

steps.title: What case could they be arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the case is. If people call the yoke צמדא and the oxen בקר, it is obvious only the yoke was sold. If they also call the oxen צמדא, then everything was sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If we say it is where people call the yoke 'צמדא' and the oxen 'בקר', it is obvious: he sold him the yoke and did not sell him the oxen! But if people also call the oxen 'צמדא', he sold him all of it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the dispute by showing that in each simple case the answer is already clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the word צמדא only means a yoke, the buyer got only the yoke, and there is nothing to argue about. If the word also means the oxen, the buyer got both. Either way, there seems to be no room for a dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are we talking about?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say where they call a yoke 'tzimda'
and oxen 'bakar', it is obvious:

phrases.aramaic: צִימְדָּא זַבֵּין לֵיהּ, בָּקָר לָא זַבֵּין לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: he sold him a yoke; oxen he did not sell him!
But rather where they also call oxen 'tzimda'?
He sold him all of it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what case the dispute from step 8 could be about
steps.kashyaTarget: The dispute between רבי יהודה and חכמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In each possible way of using the word צמדא, the answer is already clear, so there is nothing to argue about.

steps.title: A place where the word is used both ways
steps.stepSummary: The dispute is in a place where people call the yoke צמדא and the oxen בקר, but some also call the oxen צמדא. Since the word is unclear, רבי יהודה lets the price decide, and חכמים do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed in a place where people call the yoke 'צמדא' and the oxen 'בקר', but there are also some who call the oxen 'צמדא'. רבי יהודה holds that the price tells us what was meant, and the רבנן hold that the price is not proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the dispute is about a place where the word צמדא could mean either thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the word is unclear in that place, we need something else to tell us what the buyer meant. רבי יהודה uses the price for that. The רבנן do not treat the price as proof.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
in a place where they call a yoke 'tzimda'
and oxen 'bakar',
but there are also some who call oxen 'tzimda';
Rabbi Yehuda holds: The money makes it known,
and the Rabbis hold: The money is not proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, בְּאַתְרָא דְּקָרוּ לֵיהּ לְצִימְדָּא ״צִימְדָּא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by describing a third, mixed case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Sets the dispute in a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every case has an obvious answer, so there is no room for a dispute
steps.terutzMaskana: Where the word is used both ways, the meaning is unclear, so they argue over whether the price decides.

steps.title: If the price proves nothing, cancel the sale
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the רבנן: if the price is not proof and the buyer paid 200 זוז for only a yoke, the sale should be cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the price is not proof, let it be a cancelled sale!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the view of the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the price does not prove the oxen were included, the buyer paid far more than a yoke is worth. Overpaying that much should cancel the sale, so why do the רבנן just say he got the yoke?
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the oxen were sold. It is asking why, by the view of the רבנן, the deal is not cancelled entirely because of the huge overpayment.

phrases.english: But if the money is not proof,
let it be a nullified sale!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אֵין הַדָּמִים רְאָיָה, לֶיהֱוֵי בִּיטּוּל מִקָּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the view of the רבנן as explained in step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of the רבנן that the price is not proof
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Paying 200 זוז for a cheap yoke is a huge overpayment, which should cancel the sale rather than leave the buyer with just the yoke.
